answer: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease that affects bones and soft tissues around the joints. Some of the symptoms of osteoarthritis include joint pain and stiffness that can occur on one or both sides of the body, stiffness in the morning, difficulty moving the joints, and decreasing ability to carry out daily activities.
Osteoarthritis can result from years of repetitive strain on a joint, such as weight-bearing sports or repetitive uses of a joint for a long time. It can also be caused by various underlying conditions, including ethnicity, aging, and genetic factors.
Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis in adults, affecting more than 50 million U. S. adults. The condition affects people of all ages, but it is more common among older adults.
Risk factors for osteoarthritis include aging, obesity, physical activity, and genetics. Conversely, proper exercise and lowered joint weight-bearing has been shown to lower the likelihood of osteoarthritis.
